column2: On the authority of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: “I was behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day on a mount, and he said: O young man, I will teach you some words: Be mindful of Allah and He will protect you.

Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him before you. When you ask, ask Allah; and when you seek help, seek help from Allah. Know that if the nation were to gather together to benefit you with something, they would not benefit you except with something Allah has already written for you;

and if they were to gather together to harm you with something, they would not harm you except with something Allah has already written against you. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried.” Reported by al-Tirmidhī, who said: A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith. In a narration other than al-Tirmidhī's:

“Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him before you. Get to know Allah in times of ease and He will know you in times of hardship. Know that what has missed you was not going to befall you, and what has befallen you was not going to miss you. Know that victory comes with patience, relief comes with distress, and with hardship comes ease.”
Khalfa (“behind”): the opposite of in front.
ʿAlā dābbah (“on a mount”): on a donkey, riding behind the Prophet ﷺ. Yā ghulām (“O young man”): a boy from weaning until nine years of age; other views have been expressed.
“I will teach you some words”: by which Allah will benefit you. “Be mindful of Allah”: by holding constantly to fear of Him and avoiding what He has forbidden.
“He will protect you”: in yourself from what harms you. Tujāhaka (“before you”): in front of you.
“When you ask”: when you want to ask.
Istaʿanta (“you seek help”): you seek assistance.
“Seek help from Allah”: because He has power over all things. Al-ummah (“the nation”): created beings.
“Get to know Allah”: by keeping constantly to obedience to Him
“in times of ease”: in times of plenty.
“He will know you in times of hardship”: by relieving it for you.
Wa-ʿlam (“know”): a word of alerting.
“That victory”: from Allah for His servant
“comes with patience”: in obeying Allah and in His decrees that bring calamities.
Al-faraj (“relief”): coming out of worry and grief.
Al-karb (“distress”): grief and constriction. These words are near-synonyms.
It is permissible to have someone ride behind one on a mount, if it can bear it.
The command to guard the rights of Allah and the rights of created beings.
The recompense may be of the same kind as the deed.
The command to rely on Allah and put one's trust in Him rather than anyone else.
The helplessness of all created beings and their need of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
Drawing attention to the fact that the abode of this world is an abode of trial and testing, so one should be patient and content with the decision and decree.
If all created beings gathered together to harm someone or benefit him, they could do nothing that Allah had not decreed for him or against him.
The printed text reads يخسروا, evidently for يضروا (“to harm”).
Allah gives victory to the patient, and with every difficulty there is relief and a way out: “Indeed, with hardship comes ease” [al-Sharḥ 94:6].
This hadith contains a great piece of advice from the Messenger ﷺ, in which he directed [us] to keep the commands of Allah the Exalted and avoid what He has forbidden;

that Allah protects whoever does so, in his movements and his stillness, in his worldly life and his Hereafter; and that Allah, Glorified is He, is before the servant, knowing his state. So the servant should not attach his affairs and needs to anyone other than Allah;
rather, he should seek help from Allah and rely on Him in all his circumstances and affairs, except in what created beings are able to do,
in which case he asks Allah, Glorified is He, to incline their hearts towards him so that they benefit him with what they are able to do;

and that if all people gathered together and tried by their words and deeds to bring him some benefit or ward off some harm from him, or to inform him, they would not be able to harm or benefit him except by something Allah has written for him or against him;

and that if a person obeys Allah in times of ease, Allah will make for him relief and a way out in times of hardship. Let every servant be content with the good and bad that Allah has decreed for him.

In hardships and trials the servant should hold to patience, for patience is the key to relief: “Indeed, with hardship comes ease” [al-Sharḥ 94:6], and “Whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out” [al-Ṭalāq 65:2].
How many a matter has distressed me, / and then Allah brought me relief from it!
Another poet:
Do not be anxious when a matter distresses you, / and do not spend the night except with a mind at ease;
for between the blink of an eye and its opening, / Allah changes one state into another.
Another poet:
I was patient, and whoever is patient finds the outcome of his patience / sweeter and more delicious in the mouth than the bees' honey.
Another poet:
Do not be anxious over a hardship, for after it / comes ease—a promise in which there is no breach.
How many a hardship has distressed a young man when it befell him, / while within its folds were kindnesses from Allah!
